title: In‑store edge + hybrid deployment notes: retail PoC
content:
Purpose & context:
- Goal: propose and validate an architecture for a pilot deploying LLM-enabled in‑store assistant across 12 flagship stores. Evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private options with an emphasis on latency (<150ms token latency ideally), on‑device/edge inference feasibility, and customer data boundaries.

Key constraints and non‑functional requirements:
- Cold network conditions in some stores: intermittent WAN with 5–20 Mbps upstream; occasional bursting backhaul cost.
- Data residency: PII from loyalty accounts must not leave the customer VPC for >24 hours without encryption & audit.
- Latency target: 95th percentile response under 250ms for short queries (single turn, 50–150 tokens).
- Cost target for pilot: under $5k/month net infra for inference (not including development labor).
- Operational footprint: store IT will not run large GPU servers; preference for small edge boxes (e.g., T4-equivalent or CPU quantized runtimes).

High-level options considered:
A) Hosted-first (API calls to Redwood hosted):
  - Pros: fastest integration, no infra for customer to manage; immediate model upgrades & monitoring via Redwood Console.
  - Cons: higher tail latency for stores with poor WAN; potential data residency concerns unless payloads are tokenized/encrypted and retention policy enforced.
  - Fit: best for non-sensitive interactions or as a fallback when edge unavailable.

B) Dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated in customer region):
  - Pros: predictable throughput and latency SLA, isolated tenant GPUs in region close to stores; can enact VPC peering for improved security.
  - Cons: minimum commit costs; still requires reliable network connectivity from stores to region endpoints.
  - Fit: good for urban clusters of stores where network stable and cost amortizable across many stores.

C) Private / on‑prem edge inference (hybrid topology):
  - Pros: local inferencing reduces latency and WAN usage; data stays local; can operate offline.
  - Cons: customer needs small compute footprint (NVIDIA T4 / A2) or very optimized quantized CPU stacks; remote operations + lifecycle management more complex.
  - Fit: required for PII-sensitive flows or stores with highly variable network.

D) Hybrid approach (recommended pilot):
  - Local edge box running a quantized model variant for low-latency/resident-sensitive queries + Redwood hosted control plane for orchestration, metrics, and fallbacks.
  - Traffic routing policy: local first -> dedicated region -> hosted public as last resort.
  - Benefits: balances latency, cost, and data residency; enables centralized observability via secure telemetry channels.

Design options & technical tradeoffs (notes):
1) Model variants and precision
   - Option: run a distilled / 6B quantized variant on edge (8-bit or 4-bit) for most assistant intents; route longer/contextual generative flows to Dedicated.
   - Tradeoff: small model reduces quality for complex completions; mitigations include prompt engineering, intent classification, and cascading fallback to larger models in Dedicated/Hosted for escalations.

2) Caching & prefix reuse
   - Implement local prefix caching for store‑specific context (catalog chunks, store hours). Cache should be encrypted and TTL’d. Prefix reuse cuts token cost & latency.

3) KV cache synchronization
   - Lightweight periodic sync of user session KPIs to control plane for analytics. Bulk PII-scrubbed metrics only. Option to keep raw logs local and only ship diffs.

4) Network & security design
   - Use mutual TLS for control plane telemetry.
   - Local box encrypted disk; keys held in customer KMS or HSM where required.
   - Strong opt-in for shipping any user utterances; default is local-only retention until explicit consent.

5) Observability & SLOs
   - Export token-level latency histograms and model version breadcrumbs to Redwood Console.
   - Health checks: RT, GPU temp, local queue depth. Include automated rollback if 95th latency > 500ms or error rate > 2% over 10 minutes.

POC success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: 95p <= 250ms for local-first queries across 12 stores in pilot for 7 consecutive days.
- Availability: each store edge agent reports healthy > 99% during opening hours.
- Data compliance: no PII leaves local store boxes without consent or encryption; audit log produced. - Accuracy: qualitative score on 200 sample interactions; small-model intent accuracy >= 92% vs baseline.
- Cost: monthly infra cost <= $5k (pilot) including edge hardware amortization model.

Minimal viable pilot implementation plan (8 weeks):
Week 0-1: finalize scope, sign off on data residency checklist (legal & security).
Week 1-3: provisioning & PoC infra
  - Deliver 12 edge kits (Intel box + 1x T4 cloud-hosted alternative for split testing).
  - Stand up a Redwood Private control plane in customer VPC (managed instance) with telemetry endpoints.
Week 3-5: integrate model variants + routing policies
  - Deploy quantized 6B variant to edge; configure routing rules: intent classifier -> local model -> dedicated model for fallbacks.
Week 5-7: pilot QA and store rollout (staggered 3 stores / week)
Week 7-8: evaluation and decision gate (go/no-go for wider rollout).

Rough cost assumptions (pilot):
- Edge boxes (12): $2,400 month amortized (CapEx financing assumption; amortized 36 months) -> estimate $67/mo/unit
- Dedicated reserved capacity (pilot bucket): $1,800/month (small committed pool for fallback)
- Redwood Private control plane + ops: $600/month (managed fee)
- Misc (network, monitoring): $200/month
- Total: ~ $5,000/month (matches pilot target)

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: 4-bit quantization instability on certain prompt patterns -> Mitigate: maintain safe fallback to Dedicated model and add prompt sanitization.
- Risk: store IT unwilling to host edge hardware -> Mitigate: offer fully hosted pilot for subset of stores; propose 3rd-party edge managed device.
- Risk: telemetry causing PII exposure -> Mitigate: default local-only retention + strong redaction pipeline and customer KMS.

Open questions for customer/legal/security:
- What is the exact retention window allowed for user utterances before it must be purged or moved to secure vault?
- Are there stores that must be air‑gapped (no outbound connectivity) and therefore require fully on‑device workflows?
- Does the customer have an approved on‑site hardware vendor for edge devices or preferred SKUs?

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Sofia] Draft minimal data handling SLA and send to security/legal for review (target: 2024-11-15).
- [Maya] Estimate quantized model footprint for candidate 6B distilled models; bench on T4 & 8‑core CPU (target: 2024-11-12).
- [Liam] Open JIRA spike for control‑plane onboarding (JIRA-SEC-210) and diagram network flow to customer VPC.
- [Raj] Prepare a runbook for edge kit provisioning and remote updates (include rollback procedure).

Appendix: quick alternatives we rejected in discovery
- Full on-device (no control plane): high ops burden for updates and no centralized metrics — rejected for pilot.
- Pure hosted (no edge): unacceptable latency for rural stores and weak data residency guarantees.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a hybrid-first proposal to minimize both latency and privacy risk while keeping operational cost low. Feedback welcome on model choice (6B quantized vs smaller distilled 3B) and whether to front-load dedicated capacity or treat it strictly as fallback.

-- Sofia
